Original photographs are retained without cropping or color changes. Attribution, license and original-byte checks are also recorded in `sources.json`.

## Slot 2

Source: [大观园 Beijing, China (25932181142).jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%E5%A4%A7%E8%A7%82%E5%9B%AD_Beijing,_China_(25932181142).jpg). SHA-256: `5e60c10b9a9d96dc288757639209cf16f69a38fc5a4bf3d67f2b108d170acff2`. Commons SHA-1: `29fca90d1b8cde119b2141b2a3b2e9948503818c`.

The visible entrance plaque reads 蘅蕪苑 from right to left, identifying the site. A low gray barrel-tile eave, red columns and door surround, blue/green/gold painted beams and irregular ice-crack lattice flank the opening. This supports courtyard entrance, fretwork and beam construction. The cropped daylight photograph does not establish the whole courtyard, herb/rock layout, dimensions or night lighting.

## Slot 3

[ice-crack-lattice-close.jpg](ice-crack-lattice-close.jpg) — 朱華龍 - Zhu Hua Long, 2016-02-16 11:40.

Source: [大观园 Beijing, China (25419687734).jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%E5%A4%A7%E8%A7%82%E5%9B%AD_Beijing,_China_(25419687734).jpg). Photographer original: [Flickr](https://www.flickr.com/photos/mfaris01/25419687734/). License: [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0).

SHA-256: `5ca18fc7bed1e92c45352955afed1a582589ea3817c9db54905ac819a60d06a1`. Commons SHA-1: `ebe1eef9a45455509325acdb834139b1c5527a09`.

A close view of four pale painted wood screen leaves with irregular ice-crack lattice around two rectangular clear panes per leaf, carved lower panels and visible joints/hinges. It supports the Hengwu courtyard leak-window material and pattern specified in its wall kit. The photographed building is not identified as Hengwu; this is a distinguishing lattice/material reference, not site-specific architecture, plaster-rock detail or night lighting.

These are design references, not shipped textures or measured source models. All three reference slots are now collected; final scene art remains open.

## Collected night-set reference — 2026-10-08

![Night wall and lattice opening](enchanting-shadow-night-wall.png)

**The Enchanting Shadow**, exact stream PTS 53.0 seconds in the [Shaw Brothers Clips trailer](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oJ_Sy5j1XYU), uploaded 18 October 2012. The source stream is already retained in the shared trailer archive. The decoded 600 × 480 frame, decoder log and exact command/PTS are retained here. The individual frame photographer and capture date are uncredited. Copyrighted reference material; no open licence is asserted. The trailer labels the film 1959; the saved Hong Kong Film Archive record gives 1960. Both source statements remain recorded. Frame SHA-256: `0181b4387795d58f4bd187e9c23d9bd40748f41c1a5e6dab10496d3b84b890ad`.

The frame shows a figure beside broken brick/plaster masonry and a dark geometric lattice opening. Restricted blue light picks out the window and rough masonry edges; warmer brown/amber accents distinguish the near wall and costume while branches and deep openings stay near black. Night appearance is inferred visually from the directed blue light and dark setting; no shot caption supplies the time of day. It fills the generic Shaw night-set lighting/built-set slot, not Hengwu identity, its complete courtyard, herb species, perforated rocks or dimensions. No amber room lamp is visible, and the reference branches do not authorize adding trees to Hengwu's required clear skyline. Use neutral stone/plaster against limited cool fill and warm accents without copying the saturated blue source grade.

All three reference slots are now collected. Final scene art, lighting and service acceptance remain open.
